From bd903afeb504db5655a45bb4cf86f38be5b1bf62 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Song Liu <songliubraving@fb.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2018 21:55:04 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] perf/core: Fix ctx_event_type in ctx_resched()

In ctx_resched(), EVENT_FLEXIBLE should be sched_out when EVENT_PINNED is
added. However, ctx_resched() calculates ctx_event_type before checking
this condition. As a result, pinned events will NOT get higher priority
than flexible events.

The following shows this issue on an Intel CPU (where ref-cycles can
only use one hardware counter).

  1. First start:
       perf stat -C 0 -e ref-cycles  -I 1000
  2. Then, in the second console, run:
       perf stat -C 0 -e ref-cycles:D -I 1000

The second perf uses pinned events, which is expected to have higher
priority. However, because it failed in ctx_resched(). It is never
run.

This patch fixes this by calculating ctx_event_type after re-evaluating
event_type.

Reported-by: Ephraim Park <ephiepark@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Song Liu <songliubraving@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Cc: <jolsa@redhat.com>
Cc: <kernel-team@fb.com>
Cc: Alexander Shishkin <alexander.shishkin@linux.intel.com>
Cc: Arnaldo Carvalho de Melo <acme@redhat.com>
Cc: Jiri Olsa <jolsa@redhat.com>
Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
Cc: Stephane Eranian <eranian@google.com>
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Vince Weaver <vincent.weaver@maine.edu>
Fixes: 487f05e18aa4 ("perf/core: Optimize event rescheduling on active contexts")
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20180306055504.3283731-1-songliubraving@fb.com
Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/kernel/events/core.c b/kernel/events/core.c
index 96db9ae5d5af..4b838470fac4 100644
--- a/kernel/events/core.c
+++ b/kernel/events/core.c
@@ -2246,7 +2246,7 @@ static void ctx_resched(struct perf_cpu_context *cpuctx,
 			struct perf_event_context *task_ctx,
 			enum event_type_t event_type)
 {
-	enum event_type_t ctx_event_type = event_type & EVENT_ALL;
+	enum event_type_t ctx_event_type;
 	bool cpu_event = !!(event_type & EVENT_CPU);
 
 	/*
@@ -2256,6 +2256,8 @@ static void ctx_resched(struct perf_cpu_context *cpuctx,
 	if (event_type & EVENT_PINNED)
 		event_type |= EVENT_FLEXIBLE;
 
+	ctx_event_type = event_type & EVENT_ALL;
+
 	perf_pmu_disable(cpuctx->ctx.pmu);
 	if (task_ctx)
 		task_ctx_sched_out(cpuctx, task_ctx, event_type);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/events/core.c`**
- The declaration of `ctx_event_type` has been modified. It is now declared without an initial value:
  ```c
  -	enum event_type_t ctx_event_type = event_type & EVENT_ALL;
  +	enum event_type_t ctx_event_type;
  ```
- The assignment to `ctx_event_type` has been moved to a later point in the function, specifically after the check for `EVENT_PINNED`:
  ```c
  +	ctx_event_type = event_type & EVENT_ALL;
  ```

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification in `kernel/events/core.c` addresses a bug in the `ctx_resched()` function where the calculation of `ctx_event_type` was occurring before the evaluation of the `event_type` conditions. By moving the assignment of `ctx_event_type` to after the check for `EVENT_PINNED`, the patch ensures that when `EVENT_PINNED` is present, it correctly influences the scheduling priority, allowing pinned events to take precedence over flexible events. This change directly resolves the issue reported, ensuring that the event scheduling behaves as expected.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the premature calculation of `ctx_event_type` in the `ctx_resched()` function before checking if `EVENT_PINNED` was present in the `event_type`. This led to a situation where pinned events did not receive the higher priority they were supposed to have over flexible events, resulting in incorrect event scheduling behavior.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static void ctx_resched(struct perf_cpu_context *cpuctx,
 			struct perf_event_context *task_ctx,
 			enum event_type_t event_type)
 {
-	enum event_type_t ctx_event_type = event_type & EVENT_ALL;
+	enum event_type_t ctx_event_type;
 	bool cpu_event = !!(event_type & EVENT_CPU);
 
 	/*
 	 * If pinned groups are involved, flexible groups also need to be
 	 * scheduled out.
 	 */
 	if (event_type & EVENT_PINNED)
 		event_type |= EVENT_FLEXIBLE;
 
+	ctx_event_type = event_type & EVENT_ALL;
+
 	perf_pmu_disable(cpuctx->ctx.pmu);
 	if (task_ctx)
 		task_ctx_sched_out(cpuctx, task_ctx, event_type);
 
 	/*
 	 * Decide which cpu ctx groups to schedule out based on the types
 	 * of events that caused rescheduling:
 	 *  - EVENT_CPU: schedule out corresponding groups;
 	 *  - EVENT_PINNED task events: schedule out EVENT_FLEXIBLE groups;
 	 *  - otherwise, do nothing more.
 	 */
 	if (cpu_event)
 		cpu_ctx_sched_out(cpuctx, ctx_event_type);
 	else if (ctx_event_type & EVENT_PINNED)
 		cpu_ctx_sched_out(cpuctx, EVENT_FLEXIBLE);
 
 	perf_event_sched_in(cpuctx, task_ctx, current);
 	perf_pmu_enable(cpuctx->ctx.pmu);
 }
